what_its_for: Eszopiclone helps you fall asleep and stay asleep. It is used to treat insomnia, which means trouble falling asleep or waking up too often during the night. It works by calming your brain so you can get a full night of rest.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth as a tablet, just before you go to bed. Only take it when you have a full 7 to 8 hours to sleep before you need to wake up. Do not take it with a heavy, high-fat meal because this can make it work more slowly. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, split, or chew it.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 1 mg taken right before bedtime. Your doctor may increase your dose to 2 mg or 3 mg if needed. For older adults (65 and older), the starting dose is usually lower (1 mg) and should not exceed 2 mg. Always take only the dose your doctor prescribed — never take more than instructed.
missed_dose: If you forget to take your dose and you still have at least 7 to 8 hours left before you need to wake up, take it then. If you do not have enough time left to sleep a full night, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule the next night. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store eszopiclone at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep the bottle tightly closed and store it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about safe disposal options or a local medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine — combining them can cause dangerous drowsiness and breathing problems. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert the morning after taking this medicine, as it may still make you drowsy. Avoid taking other sleep aids, anxiety medicines, or sedatives unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not take it if you did not get a full night of sleep.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: sleepwalking, sleep-driving, or doing activities while asleep that you do not remember (like eating, making calls, or having sex); unusual changes in your mood or behavior; feeling confused, agitated, or aggressive; memory problems; worsening depression or thoughts of harming yourself; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also tell your doctor if your sleep does not improve after 7 to 10 days.
when_it_works: Eszopiclone usually starts working within 30 minutes of taking it. That is why you should only take it right when you are ready to go to sleep. Most people notice improvement in their sleep within the first few nights of use.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older): Use a lower dose (1 mg) because this medicine stays in your body longer and can cause more drowsiness and fall risk. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine — it may not be safe for your baby. People with liver problems: A lower dose is needed because your liver may not break down the medicine properly. People with depression or a history of substance abuse: Use with extra caution and close monitoring by your doctor.
